_about: Method-book ladder pieces (phase 8). 'pieces': per piece the title and composer (used by build-piano-library.py), the set, its order within its level (a set keeps its printed order; sets are interleaved) and study guidance; apply-learning-path.py inserts them into site/piano-curriculum.js. Levels and their evidence live in level-overrides.json. 'order': path order for pieces of the same sets that were already in the library.

burgmuller-innocence-op-100-no-5.title: L’Innocence (Innocence), Op. 100 No. 5
burgmuller-innocence-op-100-no-5.skill: Graceful slurs and a turn in 3/4
burgmuller-innocence-op-100-no-5.prerequisites: La Candeur, Op. 100 No. 1 and La Petite Réunion, No. 4.
burgmuller-innocence-op-100-no-5.pattern: A right-hand melody in short slurs with a turn figure, over left-hand broken chords in F major.
burgmuller-innocence-op-100-no-5.transfer: Lifting at the end of each slur shapes the phrase; the turn returns in La Gracieuse (No. 8).
burgmuller-innocence-op-100-no-5.exercise: Play the slurs as down-up wrist motions: weight on the first note, lift on the last.
burgmuller-innocence-op-100-no-5.check: Every slur ends lightly and the turns are even.

burgmuller-progress-op-100-no-6.title: Progrès (Progress), Op. 100 No. 6
burgmuller-progress-op-100-no-6.skill: C-major scale runs in each hand
burgmuller-progress-op-100-no-6.pattern: Running scale passages, first in the right hand then the left, with a contrasting middle and D.C. al Fine (kept as printed).
burgmuller-progress-op-100-no-6.transfer: Scale runs with smooth thumb crossings are the basis of all passagework.
burgmuller-progress-op-100-no-6.exercise: Play the run in each hand alone slowly, watching only the thumb crossing.
burgmuller-progress-op-100-no-6.check: The runs are even through each thumb crossing.

burgmuller-la-gracieuse-op-100-no-8.title: La Gracieuse (The Graceful One), Op. 100 No. 8
burgmuller-la-gracieuse-op-100-no-8.pattern: A graceful F-major melody decorated with fast turns, over left-hand chords; D.C. al Fine (kept as printed).
burgmuller-la-gracieuse-op-100-no-8.transfer: Turns like these decorate melodies by Mozart and Haydn.
burgmuller-la-gracieuse-op-100-no-8.exercise: Practise one turn as four even notes slowly, then place it before the beat it decorates.
burgmuller-la-gracieuse-op-100-no-8.check: Each turn is quick, even and does not delay the next melody note.

burgmuller-la-chasse-op-100-no-9.title: La Chasse (The Hunt), Op. 100 No. 9
burgmuller-la-chasse-op-100-no-9.pattern: Hunting-horn calls in 6/8 with staccato chords and a left hand that leaps across.
burgmuller-la-chasse-op-100-no-9.transfer: Feeling 6/8 in two big beats and placing chords cleanly are needed in every gigue and tarantella.
burgmuller-la-chasse-op-100-no-9.exercise: Count two beats per bar (ONE-and-a TWO-and-a) and play the left-hand leaps alone first.
burgmuller-la-chasse-op-100-no-9.check: The music swings in two beats per bar and the chords are short.

burgmuller-tendre-fleur-op-100-no-10.title: Tendre Fleur (Tender Flower), Op. 100 No. 10
burgmuller-tendre-fleur-op-100-no-10.pattern: D major; pairs of sixths and thirds slurred two by two, the second note light.
burgmuller-tendre-fleur-op-100-no-10.transfer: Double-note slurs train the wrist to drop and lift, needed in Schumann and Mozart.
burgmuller-tendre-fleur-op-100-no-10.exercise: Play one pair at a time: drop into the first, roll up off the second.
burgmuller-tendre-fleur-op-100-no-10.check: Every pair is down-up, and the double notes sound together.

burgmuller-la-bergeronnette-op-100-no-11.title: La Bergeronnette (The Wagtail), Op. 100 No. 11
burgmuller-la-bergeronnette-op-100-no-11.skill: Light figures passed between the hands
burgmuller-la-bergeronnette-op-100-no-11.pattern: Quick, light right-hand figures in 2/4 answered by the left hand, like a wagtail hopping.
burgmuller-la-bergeronnette-op-100-no-11.transfer: Passing a line between the hands without a bump is the basis of brilliant passages.
burgmuller-la-bergeronnette-op-100-no-11.exercise: Play the hand-overs slowly in Wait mode and listen for one continuous line.
burgmuller-la-bergeronnette-op-100-no-11.check: The line flows evenly where the hands hand over.

burgmuller-ladieu-op-100-no-12.title: L’Adieu (Farewell), Op. 100 No. 12
burgmuller-ladieu-op-100-no-12.skill: Melody and broken chords in the same hand
burgmuller-ladieu-op-100-no-12.pattern: A legato melody on the beat with broken-chord notes in between, over a bass line.
burgmuller-ladieu-op-100-no-12.transfer: Keeping a melody on top of its own accompaniment is central to Romantic piano.
burgmuller-ladieu-op-100-no-12.exercise: Play only the melody notes first, then add the broken-chord notes very softly.
burgmuller-ladieu-op-100-no-12.check: The melody is clearly louder than the notes around it.

burgmuller-consolation-op-100-no-13.title: Consolation, Op. 100 No. 13
burgmuller-consolation-op-100-no-13.skill: A singing melody over flowing left-hand chords
burgmuller-consolation-op-100-no-13.pattern: A slow C-major melody over left-hand broken chords, with a darker middle section.
burgmuller-consolation-op-100-no-13.transfer: A cantabile line over a soft accompaniment prepares nocturnes and songs without words.
burgmuller-consolation-op-100-no-13.exercise: Play the left hand alone until it is quiet and even, then add the melody.
burgmuller-consolation-op-100-no-13.check: The melody sings above a soft, even left hand.

burgmuller-la-styrienne-op-100-no-14.title: La Styrienne, Op. 100 No. 14
burgmuller-la-styrienne-op-100-no-14.skill: A Ländler with grace notes over a waltz bass
burgmuller-la-styrienne-op-100-no-14.pattern: G-major dance in 3/4 with grace notes and staccato, over a bass-chord-chord left hand; D.C. al Fine (kept as printed).
burgmuller-la-styrienne-op-100-no-14.transfer: The waltz bass and quick grace notes reappear in Schubert dances and Chopin waltzes.
burgmuller-la-styrienne-op-100-no-14.exercise: Play the left hand alone with a heavier first beat and light second and third beats.
burgmuller-la-styrienne-op-100-no-14.check: The grace notes are quick and the left hand keeps a light waltz feel.

burgmuller-douce-plainte-op-100-no-16.title: Douce Plainte (Gentle Lament), Op. 100 No. 16
burgmuller-douce-plainte-op-100-no-16.skill: An expressive melody over left-hand sixteenths
burgmuller-douce-plainte-op-100-no-16.pattern: G minor; a slow right-hand lament over a left hand moving in sixteenth notes.
burgmuller-douce-plainte-op-100-no-16.transfer: Keeping a fast accompaniment quiet under a slow melody leads to the Schumann and Chopin character pieces.
burgmuller-douce-plainte-op-100-no-16.exercise: Practise the left hand alone, quietly and evenly, before adding the melody.
burgmuller-douce-plainte-op-100-no-16.check: The left-hand sixteenths are soft and even and the melody leads.

burgmuller-la-babillarde-op-100-no-17.title: La Babillarde (The Chatterbox), Op. 100 No. 17
burgmuller-la-babillarde-op-100-no-17.pattern: Quick repeated-note and scale figures in the right hand over staccato left-hand chords.
burgmuller-la-babillarde-op-100-no-17.transfer: Light, fast fingers from the fingertips are needed in all brilliant music.
burgmuller-la-babillarde-op-100-no-17.exercise: Play the right hand at half speed, staccato, then legato, then at tempo.
burgmuller-la-babillarde-op-100-no-17.check: The chatter is light and even, never heavy.

burgmuller-inquietude-op-100-no-18.title: Inquiétude (Restlessness), Op. 100 No. 18
burgmuller-inquietude-op-100-no-18.skill: Restless sixteenth figures between the hands
burgmuller-inquietude-op-100-no-18.pattern: E minor in 2/4; short sixteenth groups tossed between the hands over sustained bass notes.
burgmuller-inquietude-op-100-no-18.transfer: Quick exchanges between the hands prepare Czerny studies and Romantic études.
burgmuller-inquietude-op-100-no-18.exercise: Practise each exchange slowly in Wait mode, then build speed with the speed trainer.
burgmuller-inquietude-op-100-no-18.check: The sixteenths are even across the hand changes.

bach-minuet-in-g-bwv-anh-116.title: Minuet in G, BWV Anh. 116 (Anna Magdalena Notebook)
bach-minuet-in-g-bwv-anh-116.skill: A longer two-voice minuet with a moving bass
bach-minuet-in-g-bwv-anh-116.pattern: Two halves (16 and 24 bars) with running eighths in the right hand over a bass that moves in quarters and halves.
bach-minuet-in-g-bwv-anh-116.transfer: Two independent voices at a steady tempo prepare the Little Preludes and Inventions.
bach-minuet-in-g-bwv-anh-116.exercise: Practise each 8-bar block hands separately, then together in Wait mode before trying In time.
bach-minuet-in-g-bwv-anh-116.check: Both voices are even and the long second half keeps the same tempo as the first.

bach-polonaise-in-f-bwv-anh-117a.title: Polonaise in F, BWV Anh. 117a (Anna Magdalena Notebook)
bach-polonaise-in-f-bwv-anh-117a.pattern: The same polonaise as Anh. 117b with more ornaments and a fuller left hand.
bach-polonaise-in-f-bwv-anh-117a.transfer: Comparing the two versions shows how ornaments decorate a simple line.
bach-polonaise-in-f-bwv-anh-117a.exercise: Play the plainer Anh. 117b version of a phrase, then this one, and listen for the added notes.
bach-polonaise-in-f-bwv-anh-117a.check: The ornaments are light and the polonaise rhythm is still clear.

bach-polonaise-in-f-bwv-anh-117b.title: Polonaise in F, BWV Anh. 117b (Anna Magdalena Notebook, plainer version)
bach-polonaise-in-f-bwv-anh-117b.skill: Polonaise rhythm in its plainer version
bach-polonaise-in-f-bwv-anh-117b.pattern: The short-short-long polonaise rhythm in 3/4 with a few ornaments, over a simple bass.
bach-polonaise-in-f-bwv-anh-117b.transfer: The notebook has this polonaise twice; this plainer version comes first, then the ornamented Anh. 117a.
bach-polonaise-in-f-bwv-anh-117b.exercise: Clap the first bar’s rhythm, then play the right hand alone keeping the dotted notes crisp.
bach-polonaise-in-f-bwv-anh-117b.check: The dotted rhythms are exact and the ornaments do not slow the beat.

bach-minuet-in-b-flat-bwv-anh-118.title: Minuet in B-flat, BWV Anh. 118 (Anna Magdalena Notebook)
bach-minuet-in-b-flat-bwv-anh-118.pattern: Two flats; right-hand eighth-note figures over a bass that moves mostly in quarters.
bach-minuet-in-b-flat-bwv-anh-118.transfer: Reading two flats securely opens up B-flat and E-flat pieces later.
bach-minuet-in-b-flat-bwv-anh-118.exercise: Before playing, mark every B and E in the score: both are flat.
bach-minuet-in-b-flat-bwv-anh-118.check: All B-flats and E-flats are correct and the minuet keeps a steady three.

bach-polonaise-in-g-minor-bwv-anh-119.title: Polonaise in G minor, BWV Anh. 119 (Anna Magdalena Notebook)
bach-polonaise-in-g-minor-bwv-anh-119.pattern: G minor with its raised F sharp, dotted polonaise rhythms and a bass that moves by step.
bach-polonaise-in-g-minor-bwv-anh-119.transfer: RCM Level 3 lists this polonaise; minor keys with a raised leading note start here.
bach-polonaise-in-g-minor-bwv-anh-119.exercise: Play the G harmonic minor scale once, then the right hand of the first phrase.
bach-polonaise-in-g-minor-bwv-anh-119.check: Every F sharp is played and the dotted rhythm stays crisp.

bach-minuet-in-a-minor-bwv-anh-120.title: Minuet in A minor, BWV Anh. 120 (Anna Magdalena Notebook)
bach-minuet-in-a-minor-bwv-anh-120.skill: A minor minuet with a trill
bach-minuet-in-a-minor-bwv-anh-120.prerequisites: Polonaise in G minor, BWV Anh. 119.
bach-minuet-in-a-minor-bwv-anh-120.pattern: A minor with G sharps, a trill near each cadence and an upbeat start to each half.
bach-minuet-in-a-minor-bwv-anh-120.transfer: RCM Level 4 lists this minuet; starting on an upbeat and closing with a trill are standard Baroque habits.
bach-minuet-in-a-minor-bwv-anh-120.exercise: Practise the trill bar slowly: four even notes, then join it into the cadence.
bach-minuet-in-a-minor-bwv-anh-120.check: Each half starts on the upbeat and the trills end in time.

bach-minuet-in-c-minor-bwv-anh-121.title: Minuet in C minor, BWV Anh. 121 (Anna Magdalena Notebook)
bach-minuet-in-c-minor-bwv-anh-121.prerequisites: Minuet in A minor, BWV Anh. 120.
bach-minuet-in-c-minor-bwv-anh-121.pattern: Three flats with B natural as the leading note; the hands often move in contrary motion.
bach-minuet-in-c-minor-bwv-anh-121.transfer: RCM Level 4 lists this minuet; three flats prepare E-flat major and C minor pieces.
bach-minuet-in-c-minor-bwv-anh-121.exercise: Play the left hand alone and listen for where it moves against the right hand.
bach-minuet-in-c-minor-bwv-anh-121.check: The B naturals are correct and the contrary motion is even in both hands.

bach-march-in-e-flat-bwv-anh-127.title: March in E-flat, BWV Anh. 127 (Anna Magdalena Notebook)
bach-march-in-e-flat-bwv-anh-127.skill: A march with triplets in E-flat
bach-march-in-e-flat-bwv-anh-127.prerequisites: Minuet in C minor, BWV Anh. 121.
bach-march-in-e-flat-bwv-anh-127.pattern: E-flat major in cut time; triplet figures mixed with even eighths over a striding bass.
bach-march-in-e-flat-bwv-anh-127.transfer: Switching between triplets and duplets in one piece is needed in Classical sonatinas.
bach-march-in-e-flat-bwv-anh-127.exercise: Clap a bar with triplets and then even eighths, counting aloud.
bach-march-in-e-flat-bwv-anh-127.check: Triplets and eighths are clearly different and the march beat stays steady.

bach-polonaise-in-d-minor-bwv-anh-128.title: Polonaise in D minor, BWV Anh. 128 (Anna Magdalena Notebook)
bach-polonaise-in-d-minor-bwv-anh-128.skill: A D minor polonaise with imitation
bach-polonaise-in-d-minor-bwv-anh-128.prerequisites: Minuet in C minor, BWV Anh. 121.
bach-polonaise-in-d-minor-bwv-anh-128.pattern: D minor with C sharps; short motifs that the left hand imitates.
bach-polonaise-in-d-minor-bwv-anh-128.transfer: RCM Level 4 lists this polonaise; hearing one hand copy the other leads to the Little Preludes.
bach-polonaise-in-d-minor-bwv-anh-128.exercise: Find each place where the left hand copies a right-hand motif and play just those bars.
bach-polonaise-in-d-minor-bwv-anh-128.check: The imitations are as clear as the melody they copy.

bach-aria-in-f-bwv-anh-131.title: Air in F, BWV Anh. 131 (Anna Magdalena Notebook)
bach-aria-in-f-bwv-anh-131.pattern: Sixteen bars: a singing right-hand line over a slower bass line, mostly quarter and eighth notes.
bach-aria-in-f-bwv-anh-131.transfer: RCM Level 1 lists this air; two independent lines lead straight into the Bach minuets.
bach-aria-in-f-bwv-anh-131.exercise: Play the bass line alone and listen to where it moves by step; then add the melody softly.
bach-aria-in-f-bwv-anh-131.check: Both lines are legato and the melody stays on top.

bach-applicatio-in-c-bwv-994.title: Applicatio in C, BWV 994 (Wilhelm Friedemann Bach Notebook)
bach-applicatio-in-c-bwv-994.skill: Bach’s own fingering with scale figures and ornaments
bach-applicatio-in-c-bwv-994.pattern: Eight bars (repeated) of C-major scale figures and ornaments, with the fingering Bach wrote for his son.
bach-applicatio-in-c-bwv-994.transfer: Applicatio means fingering: this is the first piece in Wilhelm Friedemann’s notebook, written to teach finger crossing.
bach-applicatio-in-c-bwv-994.exercise: Play each ornament slowly as written-out notes first, then at tempo.
bach-applicatio-in-c-bwv-994.check: Scale figures are even and the ornaments start on the beat.

bach-little-prelude-in-c-bwv-924.title: Little Prelude in C, BWV 924
bach-little-prelude-in-c-bwv-924.skill: Broken chords over held bass notes
bach-little-prelude-in-c-bwv-924.pattern: C major; right-hand broken-chord figures over long left-hand notes and pedal points.
bach-little-prelude-in-c-bwv-924.transfer: The first of the Little Preludes in Wilhelm Friedemann’s notebook; hearing harmonies change prepares the Prelude in C, BWV 846.
bach-little-prelude-in-c-bwv-924.exercise: Play each bar’s broken chord as a solid chord first, then as written.
bach-little-prelude-in-c-bwv-924.check: The broken chords are even and each bass note is held.

bach-little-prelude-in-d-minor-bwv-926.title: Little Prelude in D minor, BWV 926
bach-little-prelude-in-d-minor-bwv-926.skill: Broken-chord figures in 3/4 over a moving bass
bach-little-prelude-in-d-minor-bwv-926.prerequisites: Little Prelude in E minor, BWV 941.
bach-little-prelude-in-d-minor-bwv-926.pattern: D minor in 3/4: continuous right-hand broken chords over a bass line, with a sequence that climbs.
bach-little-prelude-in-d-minor-bwv-926.transfer: RCM Level 6 lists this prelude; recognising sequences makes long pieces easier to memorise.
bach-little-prelude-in-d-minor-bwv-926.exercise: Find the sequence and play one step of it as blocked chords.
bach-little-prelude-in-d-minor-bwv-926.check: The broken chords are even and the bass line is heard.

bach-little-prelude-in-f-bwv-928.title: Little Prelude in F, BWV 928
bach-little-prelude-in-f-bwv-928.prerequisites: Little Prelude in D minor, BWV 926.
bach-little-prelude-in-f-bwv-928.pattern: F major; running sixteenths in one hand answered by the other.
bach-little-prelude-in-f-bwv-928.transfer: RCM Level 8 lists this prelude; it leads straight into the two-part Inventions.
bach-little-prelude-in-f-bwv-928.exercise: Practise each hand alone with the printed slur groups, then together slowly.
bach-little-prelude-in-f-bwv-928.check: Both hands are even and the imitations are heard.

bach-little-prelude-in-d-bwv-936.title: Little Prelude in D, BWV 936
bach-little-prelude-in-d-bwv-936.skill: A two-part prelude in binary form
bach-little-prelude-in-d-bwv-936.pattern: D major in 2/4; two voices imitating each other in two repeated halves.
bach-little-prelude-in-d-bwv-936.transfer: RCM Level 8 lists this prelude; it is laid out like an Invention.
bach-little-prelude-in-d-bwv-936.exercise: Learn each half in 8-bar blocks hands separately before joining.
bach-little-prelude-in-d-bwv-936.check: Both voices are equal and the repeats are played.

bach-little-prelude-in-e-bwv-937.title: Little Prelude in E, BWV 937
bach-little-prelude-in-e-bwv-937.pattern: Four sharps; flowing sixteenth figures over a slower bass, in two repeated halves.
bach-little-prelude-in-e-bwv-937.transfer: RCM Level 8 lists this prelude; four sharps prepare E-major and C-sharp-minor pieces.
bach-little-prelude-in-e-bwv-937.exercise: Play the E-major scale, then the first phrase hands separately.
bach-little-prelude-in-e-bwv-937.check: All sharps are correct and the sixteenths are even.

bach-little-prelude-in-e-minor-bwv-938.title: Little Prelude in E minor, BWV 938
bach-little-prelude-in-e-minor-bwv-938.pattern: E minor in 3/8; one-bar figures in sixteenths passed between the hands, two repeated halves.
bach-little-prelude-in-e-minor-bwv-938.transfer: RCM Level 8 lists this prelude; the light one-in-a-bar feel is common in gigues.
bach-little-prelude-in-e-minor-bwv-938.exercise: Count one beat per bar and practise the figure changes slowly.
bach-little-prelude-in-e-minor-bwv-938.check: The music moves in one beat per bar with even sixteenths.

bach-little-prelude-in-d-minor-bwv-940.title: Little Prelude in D minor, BWV 940
bach-little-prelude-in-d-minor-bwv-940.skill: A short prelude of chords and lines
bach-little-prelude-in-d-minor-bwv-940.pattern: Ten bars in D minor mixing held chords with moving voices.
bach-little-prelude-in-d-minor-bwv-940.transfer: Short but full of harmony, it prepares the longer Little Preludes.
bach-little-prelude-in-d-minor-bwv-940.exercise: Block the harmonies bar by bar before playing the moving lines.
bach-little-prelude-in-d-minor-bwv-940.check: Held notes are held and the moving voices are clear.

bach-little-prelude-in-e-minor-bwv-941.title: Little Prelude in E minor, BWV 941
bach-little-prelude-in-e-minor-bwv-941.skill: Lines that weave between the hands
bach-little-prelude-in-e-minor-bwv-941.prerequisites: Little Prelude in D minor, BWV 940.
bach-little-prelude-in-e-minor-bwv-941.pattern: E minor in 3/4; melodic lines passed between the hands over a steady pulse.
bach-little-prelude-in-e-minor-bwv-941.transfer: RCM Level 6 lists this prelude; hearing lines in both hands prepares the Inventions.
bach-little-prelude-in-e-minor-bwv-941.exercise: Play each hand alone and mark where the melody moves to the other hand.
bach-little-prelude-in-e-minor-bwv-941.check: The line stays continuous when it passes between the hands.

bach-little-prelude-in-a-minor-bwv-942.title: Little Prelude in A minor, BWV 942
bach-little-prelude-in-a-minor-bwv-942.skill: A flowing prelude in compound time
bach-little-prelude-in-a-minor-bwv-942.prerequisites: Little Prelude in E minor, BWV 938.
bach-little-prelude-in-a-minor-bwv-942.pattern: A minor; running notes over a sustained bass, in compound time.
bach-little-prelude-in-a-minor-bwv-942.exercise: Play the bass line alone and listen to how it moves under the running notes.
bach-little-prelude-in-a-minor-bwv-942.check: The running notes are even and phrase toward each cadence.

bach-little-prelude-in-c-bwv-943.title: Little Prelude in C, BWV 943
bach-little-prelude-in-c-bwv-943.skill: A long running prelude in C
bach-little-prelude-in-c-bwv-943.prerequisites: Little Prelude in A minor, BWV 942.
bach-little-prelude-in-c-bwv-943.pattern: C major in 3/4; nearly continuous right-hand sixteenths over a slower left hand.
bach-little-prelude-in-c-bwv-943.transfer: Henle level 4; it builds the stamina needed for the Inventions.
bach-little-prelude-in-c-bwv-943.exercise: Learn it in 8-bar blocks, keeping a light hand.
bach-little-prelude-in-c-bwv-943.check: The sixteenths stay even to the end without tiring.

tchaikovsky-morning-prayer-op-39-no-1.title: Morning Prayer, Op. 39 No. 1
tchaikovsky-morning-prayer-op-39-no-1.pattern: Slow G-major chorale: four voices held and moved smoothly, with finger substitutions.
tchaikovsky-morning-prayer-op-39-no-1.transfer: RCM Level 3 lists this piece; holding some notes while others move is the basis of voice leading.
tchaikovsky-morning-prayer-op-39-no-1.exercise: Play the two hands separately, holding every tied or long note to its end.
tchaikovsky-morning-prayer-op-39-no-1.check: All four voices are legato and no held note is released early.

schumann-little-folk-song-op-68-no-9.title: Little Folk Song, Op. 68 No. 9
schumann-little-folk-song-op-68-no-9.set: Schumann, Album for the Young, Op. 68
schumann-little-folk-song-op-68-no-9.skill: A folk song with a contrasting middle section
schumann-little-folk-song-op-68-no-9.prerequisites: Melody, Op. 68 No. 1 and Humming Song, No. 3.
schumann-little-folk-song-op-68-no-9.pattern: D minor melody over chords, a brighter D-major middle part with quicker figures, then the opening again.
schumann-little-folk-song-op-68-no-9.transfer: RCM Level 5 lists this piece; changing character between sections is basic interpretation.
schumann-little-folk-song-op-68-no-9.exercise: Play the opening melody alone and decide where each phrase peaks.
schumann-little-folk-song-op-68-no-9.check: The two sections sound different in character and the return matches the opening.

schumann-may-dear-may-op-68-no-13.title: May, Dear May, Soon You’ll Be Here Again, Op. 68 No. 13
schumann-may-dear-may-op-68-no-13.set: Schumann, Album for the Young, Op. 68
schumann-may-dear-may-op-68-no-13.skill: A melody with syncopated inner voices
schumann-may-dear-may-op-68-no-13.pattern: E major in 2/4; a melody on top with inner voices and syncopated accompaniment in both hands.
schumann-may-dear-may-op-68-no-13.transfer: Henle level 5; voicing a melody over inner parts is central to Romantic piano.
schumann-may-dear-may-op-68-no-13.exercise: Play the melody alone, then add the inner voices very softly.
schumann-may-dear-may-op-68-no-13.check: The melody is clearly on top and the syncopations stay in time.

streabbog-les-etoiles-dor-no-1-valse.title: Les étoiles d’or No. 1 · Valse
streabbog-les-etoiles-dor-no-1-valse.skill: A salon waltz with an oom-pah-pah bass
streabbog-les-etoiles-dor-no-1-valse.pattern: C-major waltz: quarter-note melody with grace notes over a bass note and two chords per bar; D.S. al Fine (kept as printed).
streabbog-les-etoiles-dor-no-1-valse.transfer: This bass pattern is the accompaniment of every waltz; the melody uses printed fingering.
streabbog-les-etoiles-dor-no-1-valse.exercise: Play the left hand alone, low note slightly heavier, chords light.
streabbog-les-etoiles-dor-no-1-valse.check: The melody is above the accompaniment and the waltz feels one beat per bar.

behr-in-may.title: In May
behr-in-may.skill: A five-finger tune over broken-chord bass in 3/4
behr-in-may.pattern: A right-hand tune in C position over a left hand that outlines C–E–G and B–F–G chords, three quarters a bar.
behr-in-may.transfer: The left-hand pattern is the tonic and dominant-seventh shape you will meet in every accompaniment.
behr-in-may.exercise: Play the left hand alone and name the two chord shapes, then add the tune.
behr-in-may.check: The left hand stays soft and even under a singing tune for all 32 bars.

beyer-op-101-no-12.title: Exercise No. 12, Op. 101
beyer-op-101-no-12.skill: Right-hand five-finger walk over long bass notes
beyer-op-101-no-12.pattern: The right hand walks C–D–E–F–G and back in quarter notes; the left hand holds C and G whole notes.
beyer-op-101-no-12.transfer: A moving melody over a held bass is the most common piano texture, from folk songs to Mozart.
beyer-op-101-no-12.exercise: Play the left hand whole notes alone, then the right hand alone; join them in Wait mode, letting each bass note ring for four beats.
beyer-op-101-no-12.check: Each left-hand note is held for the whole bar while the right hand keeps moving evenly.

beyer-op-101-no-13.title: Exercise No. 13, Op. 101
beyer-op-101-no-13.skill: Left-hand five-finger walk under a held melody
beyer-op-101-no-13.pattern: The same walk as No. 12, but now the left hand moves in quarter notes and the right hand holds C and G.
beyer-op-101-no-13.transfer: Most beginners lead with the right hand; this gives the left hand the busy part.
beyer-op-101-no-13.exercise: Practise the left hand alone until it is even, then add the right hand whole notes.
beyer-op-101-no-13.check: The left hand stays even and the right hand still sounds for four beats each bar.

beyer-op-101-no-14.title: Exercise No. 14, Op. 101
beyer-op-101-no-14.skill: A first repeat sign and a broken-chord ending
beyer-op-101-no-14.pattern: Four bars that repeat, then four bars that finish with C–G–C–G in both hands.
beyer-op-101-no-14.transfer: Repeat signs appear in almost every dance and minuet; following them is part of reading the score.
beyer-op-101-no-14.exercise: Find the repeat sign before you start and point to where the music goes back.
beyer-op-101-no-14.check: I play the first four bars twice and the ending once without stopping.

beyer-op-101-no-15.title: Exercise No. 15, Op. 101
beyer-op-101-no-15.skill: Two eight-bar halves with a repeated second half
beyer-op-101-no-15.pattern: Right-hand steps in quarters over a slow left hand; the second half repeats and has a dotted half note.
beyer-op-101-no-15.transfer: Two-part form with a repeat is the shape of the minuets at Level 2 and 3.
beyer-op-101-no-15.exercise: Play the left hand alone and count the dotted half for three beats; then hands together.
beyer-op-101-no-15.check: The dotted half note gets three beats and both halves flow without a gap.

beyer-op-101-no-24.title: Child’s Song (Summ, summ, summ), Op. 101 No. 24
beyer-op-101-no-24.skill: A folk song with a walking left hand
beyer-op-101-no-24.pattern: The tune Summ, summ, summ in the right hand over a left hand that moves in steady quarter notes, legato.
beyer-op-101-no-24.transfer: Two moving lines at once is the next step after held bass notes.
beyer-op-101-no-24.exercise: Sing or hum the tune, then play the left hand alone legato before joining the hands slowly.
beyer-op-101-no-24.check: Both hands are legato and the tune is louder than the left hand.

beyer-op-101-no-25.title: Exercise No. 25 in 3/4, Op. 101
beyer-op-101-no-25.pattern: The right hand plays a phrase while the left hand rests, then the left hand answers; the second half repeats.
beyer-op-101-no-25.transfer: Passing a phrase between the hands trains listening for the line rather than the hand.
beyer-op-101-no-25.exercise: Count the left hand’s rest bars aloud; play the answers in Wait mode first.
beyer-op-101-no-25.check: No beat is lost where one hand takes over from the other.

beyer-op-101-no-38.title: Child’s Song (A, a, a, der Winter), Op. 101 No. 38
beyer-op-101-no-38.prerequisites: Beyer No. 25 and the G position (right thumb on G).
beyer-op-101-no-38.pattern: A children’s song in G position, played non legato (detached), over a quarter-note left hand.
beyer-op-101-no-38.transfer: Moving the whole hand to a new position and changing touch on purpose are two key beginner skills.
beyer-op-101-no-38.exercise: Place both hands in G position before starting; play every note slightly detached.
beyer-op-101-no-38.check: The notes are detached but even, and the song keeps a steady beat.

beyer-op-101-no-39.title: Exercise No. 39 in G position, Op. 101
beyer-op-101-no-39.skill: Half-note melody over a quarter-note bass in G position
beyer-op-101-no-39.pattern: A slurred half-note melody in G position with the left hand alternating low notes and D; the last line has quarter notes.
beyer-op-101-no-39.transfer: RCM Preparatory A lists Beyer No. 39; it joins legato melody and a steady accompaniment.
beyer-op-101-no-39.exercise: Play the left-hand pattern alone (low note, D, low note, D) until it is automatic, then add the melody.
beyer-op-101-no-39.check: The melody is legato across each slur and the left hand stays quiet and even.

gurlitt-op-117-no-1.title: The First Lessons, Op. 117 No. 1
gurlitt-op-117-no-1.skill: Legato half-note pairs with a slow bass
gurlitt-op-117-no-1.pattern: Half-note pairs in the right hand (C–E, D–G…) over whole notes in the left hand; the second half slurs the pairs.
gurlitt-op-117-no-1.transfer: Gurlitt’s first lesson is a real little piece: listen for the slurs and the quiet dynamic.
gurlitt-op-117-no-1.exercise: Play the second half’s slurred pairs slowly, lifting at the end of each slur.
gurlitt-op-117-no-1.check: Each slurred pair is connected, with a small lift before the next pair.

kohler-op-190-no-2.title: Very Easy Piece, Op. 190 No. 2
kohler-op-190-no-2.skill: Half notes moving by steps and skips in C position
kohler-op-190-no-2.prerequisites: Both thumbs on a C (right hand C5, left hand middle C) and the Level 0 First keys pieces.
kohler-op-190-no-2.pattern: Both hands play the same note names an octave apart in half notes: up a third, back by step, one long C to finish.
kohler-op-190-no-2.transfer: Reading the same shape in two clefs-worth of space at once is the first step to hands together; the printed finger numbers match the C position.
kohler-op-190-no-2.exercise: Play the right hand alone saying the finger numbers, then the left hand alone; then both together in Wait mode.
kohler-op-190-no-2.check: Both hands land on each new note together for all eight bars.

kohler-op-190-no-3.title: Very Easy Piece in 3/4, Op. 190 No. 3
kohler-op-190-no-3.skill: Quarter notes and half notes in 3/4
kohler-op-190-no-3.pattern: Eight bars of ONE-two-three: a quarter-note skip E–G–E, then half note plus quarter, both hands in octaves.
kohler-op-190-no-3.transfer: Counting a half note as two beats inside a three-beat bar prepares every minuet and waltz.
kohler-op-190-no-3.exercise: Clap the rhythm counting ONE-two-three, then play it hands together slowly.
kohler-op-190-no-3.check: Every half note lasts two full beats and the last bar has its quarter rest.

kohler-op-190-no-4.title: Very Easy Piece, Op. 190 No. 4
kohler-op-190-no-4.skill: Mixed quarters and halves, hands in octaves
kohler-op-190-no-4.pattern: Two quarters and a half note in most bars, with one bar of four quarters reaching G (finger 5).
kohler-op-190-no-4.transfer: Mixing note lengths inside one phrase is what real melodies do; the hands still move in the same direction.
kohler-op-190-no-4.exercise: Play each bar as a small group: short-short-long. Say the fingers aloud before playing.
kohler-op-190-no-4.check: The quarters are even and the halves are held, with no pause at the bar lines.

kohler-op-190-no-5.title: Very Easy Piece (contrary motion), Op. 190 No. 5
kohler-op-190-no-5.pattern: Whole notes only, but the right hand climbs while the left hand goes down, ending a sixth apart.
kohler-op-190-no-5.transfer: Contrary motion trains each hand to read its own line, the basis of every two-part piece.
kohler-op-190-no-5.exercise: Read the left hand alone first, naming the finger numbers, then add the right hand one bar at a time.
kohler-op-190-no-5.check: I can play all 16 bars hands together without looking at my hands.

kohler-op-190-no-27.title: Study in F, Op. 190 No. 27
kohler-op-190-no-27.skill: Melody over left-hand broken chords in F
kohler-op-190-no-27.prerequisites: Köhler Op. 218 No. 36 and B-flat in F major.
kohler-op-190-no-27.pattern: A dotted-half melody over a left hand that plays F–A–C (and its neighbours) in quarters every bar; a B natural and F sharp appear.
kohler-op-190-no-27.transfer: RCM Level 2 lists this étude; holding a melody note while the other hand moves is the core of accompaniment.
kohler-op-190-no-27.exercise: Play the left hand alone and say the chord names (F, D minor, C, B-flat…), then add the long right-hand notes.
kohler-op-190-no-27.check: Each long melody note is held for three beats over an even left hand, and the B natural and F sharp are correct.

kohler-op-218-no-36.title: Melody in F (Steirisch), Op. 218 No. 36
kohler-op-218-no-36.skill: A Styrian dance with accented downbeats and staccato chords
kohler-op-218-no-36.prerequisites: Köhler Op. 218 No. 32 and two-note chords in each hand.
kohler-op-218-no-36.pattern: Accented low note then two staccato chords in the right hand, over bass note plus chords; both halves repeat with first and second endings.
kohler-op-218-no-36.transfer: RCM Level 1 lists this Melodie; accent-then-light is the feel of every waltz and Ländler.
kohler-op-218-no-36.exercise: Play the right hand of bars 3–4 alone: lean on the accented note, then make the two chords short and light.
kohler-op-218-no-36.check: The accents are clear, the chords are short, and the first and second endings are taken correctly.

gurlitt-op-117-no-2.title: The First Lessons, Op. 117 No. 2
gurlitt-op-117-no-2.skill: Quarter-note melody in C position with a dynamic plan
gurlitt-op-117-no-2.pattern: Right-hand quarters C–E–G–E over a left hand of whole and half notes; the second part repeats F–E–D–E with a crescendo back to forte.
gurlitt-op-117-no-2.transfer: Following printed dynamics (f, mf, crescendo) on a simple tune is the first step from playing notes to making music.
gurlitt-op-117-no-2.exercise: Play the second part three times: mf, then growing louder each bar, arriving forte at the return.
gurlitt-op-117-no-2.check: The f, mf and crescendo are clearly different and both repeats are played.

gurlitt-op-117-no-3.title: The First Lessons, Op. 117 No. 3
gurlitt-op-117-no-3.skill: Melody moving from the right hand to the left hand in 3/4
gurlitt-op-117-no-3.pattern: Three-note steps C–D–E rising and falling, first in the right hand over held C, then in the left hand under a held C, then in both hands together.
gurlitt-op-117-no-3.transfer: Passing the same figure from one hand to the other, then doubling it, builds equal hands.
gurlitt-op-117-no-3.exercise: Play bars 9–16 left hand alone until the figure sounds as smooth as in the right hand.
gurlitt-op-117-no-3.check: The held notes last their full value and the last section is hands together in time.

gurlitt-op-117-no-4.title: The First Lessons, Op. 117 No. 4
gurlitt-op-117-no-4.skill: Half notes in thirds and sixths between the hands, with first and second endings
gurlitt-op-117-no-4.pattern: Both hands play half notes a sixth or a third apart; a crescendo and diminuendo shape the phrase, then first and second endings.
gurlitt-op-117-no-4.transfer: First and second endings appear in most folk songs and dances; the hands move in parallel, an early step to harmony.
gurlitt-op-117-no-4.exercise: Point to the first and second ending before playing; then play the piece once without stopping.
gurlitt-op-117-no-4.check: I take the first ending, repeat, and finish with the second ending, with a clear swell in the middle.

kohler-op-218-no-32.title: Melody in G (Waltz), Op. 218 No. 32
kohler-op-218-no-32.skill: A waltz: staccato melody over bass-and-chord accompaniment in G
kohler-op-218-no-32.prerequisites: The Level 1 Beyer and Köhler pieces, and F sharp in G major.
kohler-op-218-no-32.pattern: Upbeat pairs and staccato quarters over a left hand of bass note and two-note chords; a legato middle passage with broken chords and C sharp.
kohler-op-218-no-32.transfer: The waltz bass (low note, then two light chords) is the accompaniment of every waltz and minuet.
kohler-op-218-no-32.exercise: Play the left hand alone, low note slightly heavier, chords short and light; then add the melody.
kohler-op-218-no-32.check: The staccato notes are short, the legato passage is smooth, and both halves repeat.

czerny-op-139-no-1.title: Progressive Study, Op. 139 No. 1
czerny-op-139-no-1.skill: Right-hand thirds over a broken-chord left hand
czerny-op-139-no-1.prerequisites: Reading two-note chords in one hand; Köhler Op. 190 No. 27.
czerny-op-139-no-1.pattern: Two 8-bar halves, each repeated: right-hand half notes and thirds in quarters, over a left hand that alternates bass notes and G.
czerny-op-139-no-1.transfer: The first study of Czerny’s Op. 139 (RCM Level 2 lists No. 33 of the set); playing thirds evenly prepares double notes in later études.
czerny-op-139-no-1.exercise: Play the right-hand thirds alone, listening that both notes of each third sound together.
czerny-op-139-no-1.check: Every third is together and the left hand stays quiet and even.
